title: Your Fertiliser Bill Just Got a Helping Hand: Understanding the Rabi Subsidy

faq.a: The Rabi season refers to the winter cropping season in India. Crops are sown from October to December and harvested from April to June. Key Rabi crops include wheat, barley, oats, gram, mustard, and linseed.

P&K stands for Phosphatic and Potassic fertilisers. These are essential plant nutrients, specifically Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K), which are crucial for plant growth, root development, flowering, and overall crop health. DAP (Di-ammonium Phosphate) and MOP (Muriate of Potash) are common examples.

faq.q: How does the subsidy amount change each year?
faq.a: The government reviews the Nutrient-Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for P&K fertilisers before each cropping season (Kharif and Rabi). These rates are adjusted based on factors like international prices of raw materials, the exchange rate, and the prevailing market conditions to ensure the fertilisers remain affordable for farmers.

faq.q: Does this subsidy cover all types of fertilisers?
faq.a: No, the Nutrient-Based Subsidy (NBS) specifically covers phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers. Urea, another major fertiliser, has a separate subsidy mechanism where its Maximum Retail Price (MRP) is fixed by the government.

faq.q: How does this affect the environment?
faq.a: The Nutrient-Based Subsidy encourages balanced fertilisation, as farmers are incentivised to use P&K fertilisers along with urea. This can help improve soil health and reduce the overuse of a single nutrient, contributing to more sustainable agricultural practices.
